_readme: Hostile SQL for the schema_context join grant (JOIN-GRANT-SUBQUERY-01, #408). Each case relates two tables the caller declared. Replayed by tests/dms/test_join_grant_subquery_408.py against CortexOS.insights.schema_context.ungranted_reason and against POST /v1/insights. Cases may be added. A case never moves from a refusal to 'decided_granted'.

_expected_values.refuse_ungranted_join: refused by name (schema_context:ungranted_join:<left>+<right>) under 'schema'; the same SQL passes the join decision under 'control_schema', where the JOINS line exists
_expected_values.envelope=refused_before_the_gate: the route's statement extractor does not accept the statement, so the gate never sees it; the envelope is still a REFUSE with no SQL
_expected_values.refuse_unanalysable: refused as schema_context:unanalysable_join under every schema: the statement reads a relation the join decision cannot name
_expected_values.envelope_reason: what the consumer reads for a refuse_unanalysable case: the SQL gate's own name for the statement. If the SQL gate has no name for it the consumer reads schema_context:unanalysable_join

schemas.pair_no_join:
SCHEMA
- alpha_ledger
- id integer
- qty integer
- beta_entry
- ref_code integer
- amt integer
schemas.pair_joined:
SCHEMA
- alpha_ledger
- id integer
- qty integer
- beta_entry
- ref_code integer
- amt integer
JOINS
- alpha_ledger.id = beta_entry.ref_code (ledger_entry)
schemas.chain:
SCHEMA
- alpha_ledger
- id integer
- qty integer
- beta_entry
- ref_code integer
- amt integer
- gamma_note
- entry_ref integer
- note text
JOINS
- alpha_ledger.id = beta_entry.ref_code (ledger_entry)
- beta_entry.ref_code = gamma_note.entry_ref (entry_note)
schemas.chain_all:
SCHEMA
- alpha_ledger
- id integer
- qty integer
- beta_entry
- ref_code integer
- amt integer
- gamma_note
- entry_ref integer
- note text
JOINS
- alpha_ledger.id = beta_entry.ref_code (ledger_entry)
- beta_entry.ref_code = gamma_note.entry_ref (entry_note)
- alpha_ledger.id = gamma_note.entry_ref (ledger_note)

cases.name: cte_join
cases.sql: WITH x AS (SELECT id, qty FROM alpha_ledger WHERE qty > 1) SELECT x.qty, b.amt FROM x JOIN beta_entry b ON x.id = b.ref_code WHERE b.amt > 0
cases.why_it_might_slip: The JOIN's left operand is a CTE name, so a check that pairs named tables sees one table and no pair.

cases.name: cte_both_sides
cases.sql: WITH x AS (SELECT id, qty FROM alpha_ledger WHERE qty > 1), y AS (SELECT ref_code, amt FROM beta_entry WHERE amt > 0) SELECT x.qty, y.amt FROM x JOIN y ON x.id = y.ref_code WHERE x.qty > 2
cases.why_it_might_slip: Both operands are CTE names. No named table appears in any JOIN.

cases.name: cte_named_like_the_table_it_wraps
cases.sql: WITH beta_entry AS (SELECT ref_code, amt FROM beta_entry WHERE amt > 0) SELECT a.qty, beta_entry.amt FROM alpha_ledger a JOIN beta_entry ON a.id = beta_entry.ref_code WHERE a.qty > 1
cases.why_it_might_slip: The CTE carries the table's own name. A check that exempts every name found in a WITH list exempts the joined table.

cases.name: cte_in_other_scope_exempts_a_direct_join
cases.sql: SELECT a.qty, b.amt FROM alpha_ledger a JOIN beta_entry b ON a.id = b.ref_code WHERE a.qty > (WITH beta_entry AS (SELECT 1 AS x) SELECT x FROM beta_entry)
cases.why_it_might_slip: A CTE declared inside a scalar subquery is invisible to the outer JOIN, which reads the real table. WITH names collected from the whole tree exempt it anyway.

cases.name: cte_chain_three_deep
cases.sql: WITH x AS (SELECT id, qty FROM alpha_ledger WHERE qty > 1), y AS (SELECT id, qty FROM x WHERE qty > 2), z AS (SELECT y.qty, b.amt FROM y JOIN beta_entry b ON y.id = b.ref_code WHERE b.amt > 0) SELECT qty, amt FROM z WHERE qty > 3
cases.why_it_might_slip: The table is two CTE hops away from the JOIN that relates it.

cases.name: derived_table_join
cases.sql: SELECT d.qty, b.amt FROM (SELECT id, qty FROM alpha_ledger WHERE qty > 1) d JOIN beta_entry b ON d.id = b.ref_code WHERE b.amt > 0
cases.why_it_might_slip: The FROM operand is a subquery, which has no table name to pair.

cases.name: derived_table_on_the_join_side
cases.sql: SELECT a.qty, d.amt FROM alpha_ledger a JOIN (SELECT ref_code, amt FROM beta_entry WHERE amt > 0) d ON a.id = d.ref_code WHERE a.qty > 1
cases.why_it_might_slip: The JOIN operand is a subquery.

cases.name: derived_table_nested_three_deep
cases.sql: SELECT d3.qty, b.amt FROM (SELECT id, qty FROM (SELECT id, qty FROM (SELECT id, qty FROM alpha_ledger WHERE qty > 1) d1 WHERE qty > 2) d2 WHERE qty > 3) d3 JOIN beta_entry b ON d3.id = b.ref_code WHERE b.amt > 0
cases.why_it_might_slip: Nesting depth: the table sits three subqueries below the JOIN.

cases.name: comma_join_with_derived_table
cases.sql: SELECT a.qty, d.amt FROM alpha_ledger a, (SELECT ref_code, amt FROM beta_entry WHERE amt > 0) d WHERE a.id = d.ref_code
cases.why_it_might_slip: A comma join has no JOIN keyword and its right operand is a subquery.

cases.name: parenthesised_join_operand
cases.sql: SELECT a.qty, b.amt FROM (alpha_ledger a JOIN beta_entry b ON a.id = b.ref_code) WHERE a.qty > 1
cases.why_it_might_slip: The whole join sits inside parentheses, so the outer FROM holds one unnamed operand.

cases.name: semi_join_on_derived_table
cases.sql: SELECT a.qty FROM alpha_ledger a SEMI JOIN (SELECT ref_code FROM beta_entry WHERE amt > 0) d ON a.id = d.ref_code WHERE a.qty > 1
cases.why_it_might_slip: DuckDB SEMI JOIN against a subquery: an existence probe with no named right table.

cases.name: natural_join_on_derived_table
cases.sql: SELECT qty FROM alpha_ledger NATURAL JOIN (SELECT ref_code AS id FROM beta_entry WHERE amt > 0) d WHERE qty > 1
cases.why_it_might_slip: NATURAL JOIN has no ON clause and the operand is a subquery that renames the key.

cases.name: in_subquery
cases.sql: SELECT qty FROM alpha_ledger WHERE id IN (SELECT ref_code FROM beta_entry WHERE amt > 0)
cases.why_it_might_slip: IN is a semi-join written in WHERE. No JOIN clause exists.

cases.name: not_in_subquery
cases.sql: SELECT qty FROM alpha_ledger WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT ref_code FROM beta_entry WHERE amt > 0)
cases.why_it_might_slip: The anti-join form of the same probe.

cases.name: any_subquery
cases.sql: SELECT qty FROM alpha_ledger WHERE id = ANY (SELECT ref_code FROM beta_entry WHERE amt > 0)
cases.why_it_might_slip: = ANY is IN under another spelling.

cases.name: in_subquery_inside_join_on
cases.sql: SELECT l.qty FROM alpha_ledger l JOIN alpha_ledger r ON l.id = r.id AND l.id IN (SELECT ref_code FROM beta_entry WHERE amt > 0) WHERE l.qty > 1
cases.why_it_might_slip: The JOIN is a granted self-join. The other table hides in its ON condition.

cases.name: exists_correlated
cases.sql: SELECT a.qty FROM alpha_ledger a WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM beta_entry b WHERE b.ref_code = a.id)
cases.why_it_might_slip: A correlated EXISTS joins row by row with no JOIN clause.

cases.name: not_exists_correlated
cases.sql: SELECT a.qty FROM alpha_ledger a WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM beta_entry b WHERE b.ref_code = a.id)
cases.why_it_might_slip: The anti-join form.

cases.name: scalar_subquery_correlated_in_select
cases.sql: SELECT a.qty, (SELECT max(b.amt) FROM beta_entry b WHERE b.ref_code = a.id) AS top_amt FROM alpha_ledger a WHERE a.qty > 1
cases.why_it_might_slip: The second table is read from the SELECT list.

cases.name: scalar_subquery_uncorrelated_in_where
cases.sql: SELECT qty FROM alpha_ledger WHERE qty > (SELECT avg(amt) FROM beta_entry)
cases.why_it_might_slip: No correlation and no JOIN, yet each row is compared with a value computed from the other table.

cases.name: subquery_in_having
cases.sql: SELECT id, sum(qty) AS total FROM alpha_ledger GROUP BY id HAVING sum(qty) > (SELECT max(amt) FROM beta_entry WHERE amt > 0)
cases.why_it_might_slip: HAVING is walked less often than WHERE.

cases.name: subquery_in_order_by
cases.sql: SELECT a.qty FROM alpha_ledger a WHERE a.qty > 1 ORDER BY (SELECT max(b.amt) FROM beta_entry b WHERE b.ref_code = a.id)
cases.why_it_might_slip: The sort key leaks the other table's ordering.

cases.name: subquery_in_aggregate_filter
cases.sql: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE id IN (SELECT ref_code FROM beta_entry WHERE amt > 0)) AS n FROM alpha_ledger
cases.why_it_might_slip: The probe sits in an aggregate FILTER clause.

cases.name: subquery_in_case_expression
cases.sql: SELECT a.qty, CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM beta_entry b WHERE b.ref_code = a.id) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_entry FROM alpha_ledger a WHERE a.qty > 1
cases.why_it_might_slip: The existence probe is a CASE branch in the SELECT list.

cases.name: subquery_in_qualify
cases.sql: SELECT a.qty FROM alpha_ledger a WHERE a.qty > 1 QUALIFY row_number() OVER (ORDER BY a.qty) <= (SELECT count(*) FROM beta_entry WHERE amt > 0)
cases.why_it_might_slip: QUALIFY is a DuckDB clause a walker of WHERE and HAVING never visits.

cases.name: subquery_in_limit
cases.sql: SELECT qty FROM alpha_ledger WHERE qty > 1 LIMIT (SELECT count(*) FROM beta_entry WHERE amt > 0)
cases.why_it_might_slip: The row count of the answer becomes the other table's count.

cases.name: union_top_level
cases.sql: SELECT qty FROM alpha_ledger WHERE qty > 1 UNION ALL SELECT amt FROM beta_entry WHERE amt > 0
cases.why_it_might_slip: A set operation stacks two tables in one result with no JOIN anywhere.

cases.name: intersect_top_level
cases.sql: SELECT id FROM alpha_ledger WHERE qty > 1 INTERSECT SELECT ref_code FROM beta_entry WHERE amt > 0
cases.why_it_might_slip: INTERSECT is an equi-join on the whole row.

cases.name: except_top_level
cases.sql: SELECT id FROM alpha_ledger WHERE qty > 1 EXCEPT SELECT ref_code FROM beta_entry WHERE amt > 0
cases.why_it_might_slip: EXCEPT is an anti-join on the whole row.

cases.name: union_inside_derived_table
cases.sql: SELECT u.v FROM (SELECT qty AS v FROM alpha_ledger WHERE qty > 1 UNION ALL SELECT amt AS v FROM beta_entry WHERE amt > 0) u WHERE u.v > 0
cases.why_it_might_slip: The statement is a SELECT, so a check for a top-level set operation passes it.

cases.name: union_inside_cte
cases.sql: WITH u AS (SELECT qty AS v FROM alpha_ledger WHERE qty > 1 UNION SELECT amt AS v FROM beta_entry WHERE amt > 0) SELECT v FROM u WHERE v > 0
cases.why_it_might_slip: The set operation is a CTE body.

cases.name: union_by_name
cases.sql: SELECT qty AS v FROM alpha_ledger WHERE qty > 1 UNION ALL BY NAME SELECT amt AS v FROM beta_entry WHERE amt > 0
cases.why_it_might_slip: DuckDB UNION BY NAME.

cases.name: lateral_correlated_subquery
cases.sql: SELECT a.qty, x.total FROM alpha_ledger a, LATERAL (SELECT sum(b.amt) AS total FROM beta_entry b WHERE b.ref_code = a.id) x WHERE a.qty > 1
cases.why_it_might_slip: LATERAL is a correlated join whose operand is a subquery.

cases.name: left_join_lateral
cases.sql: SELECT a.qty, x.amt FROM alpha_ledger a LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT b.amt FROM beta_entry b WHERE b.ref_code = a.id LIMIT 1) x ON true WHERE a.qty > 1
cases.why_it_might_slip: JOIN LATERAL ... ON true: the ON clause says nothing and the correlation is inside.

cases.name: from_first_derived_table
cases.sql: FROM (FROM alpha_ledger SELECT id, qty WHERE qty > 1) d JOIN beta_entry b ON d.id = b.ref_code SELECT d.qty, b.amt WHERE b.amt > 0
cases.why_it_might_slip: DuckDB FROM-first syntax around a derived table.

cases.name: pivot_operand_joined
cases.sql: SELECT b.amt FROM (PIVOT alpha_ledger ON qty USING count(*) GROUP BY id) p JOIN beta_entry b ON p.id = b.ref_code WHERE b.amt > 0
cases.why_it_might_slip: The FROM operand is a PIVOT statement in parentheses.

cases.name: columns_expression_over_cte
cases.sql: WITH x AS (SELECT id, qty FROM alpha_ledger WHERE qty > 1) SELECT COLUMNS('.*') FROM x JOIN beta_entry b ON x.id = b.ref_code WHERE b.amt > 0
cases.why_it_might_slip: COLUMNS() names no column, and the JOIN's left operand is a CTE.

cases.name: quoted_mixed_case_through_cte
cases.sql: WITH x AS (SELECT id, qty FROM "ALPHA_LEDGER" WHERE qty > 1) SELECT x.qty, b.amt FROM x JOIN "Beta_Entry" b ON x.id = b.ref_code WHERE b.amt > 0
cases.why_it_might_slip: DuckDB folds quoted ASCII names to the same table. A pair compared without the fold never matches a refusal.

cases.name: schema_qualified_in_subquery
cases.sql: SELECT qty FROM main.alpha_ledger WHERE id IN (SELECT ref_code FROM main.beta_entry WHERE amt > 0)
cases.why_it_might_slip: Qualified names compare by bare name; the pair must still be found.

cases.name: cte_name_differs_only_by_case
cases.sql: WITH Beta_Entry AS (SELECT 1 AS ref_code) SELECT a.qty FROM alpha_ledger a WHERE a.id IN (SELECT ref_code FROM main.beta_entry WHERE amt > 0)
cases.why_it_might_slip: A CTE spelled like the table. The qualified reference reaches the real table, never the CTE.

cases.name: chain_skips_the_bridge_table
cases.sql: WITH x AS (SELECT id, qty FROM alpha_ledger WHERE qty > 1) SELECT x.qty, g.note FROM x JOIN gamma_note g ON x.id = g.entry_ref WHERE g.note IS NOT NULL
cases.why_it_might_slip: alpha-beta and beta-gamma are granted. alpha-gamma is not, and beta is not in the statement.

cases.name: chain_skips_the_bridge_table_in_subquery
cases.sql: SELECT note FROM gamma_note WHERE entry_ref IN (SELECT id FROM alpha_ledger WHERE qty > 1)
cases.why_it_might_slip: The same ungranted pair, as an IN probe.

cases.name: table_function_reads_a_table_by_string
cases.sql: SELECT a.qty, b.amt FROM alpha_ledger a JOIN query_table('beta_entry') b ON a.id = b.ref_code WHERE a.qty > 1
cases.why_it_might_slip: query_table() takes the table name as a string, so no table reference exists to pair.

cases.name: table_function_inside_in_subquery
cases.sql: SELECT qty FROM alpha_ledger WHERE id IN (SELECT ref_code FROM query_table('beta_entry') WHERE amt > 0)
cases.why_it_might_slip: The same string-named read, one scope down.

cases.name: lateral_table_function
cases.sql: SELECT a.qty FROM alpha_ledger a, LATERAL query_table('beta_entry') b WHERE a.id = b.ref_code
cases.why_it_might_slip: LATERAL f() hangs the call off a Lateral node, not a Table node.

cases.name: query_function_runs_sql_from_a_string
cases.sql: SELECT a.qty FROM alpha_ledger a JOIN query('SELECT ref_code FROM beta_entry') b ON a.id = b.ref_code WHERE a.qty > 1
cases.why_it_might_slip: query() runs a whole statement held in a string literal.

cases.name: recursive_cte
cases.sql: WITH RECURSIVE r AS (SELECT id, qty FROM alpha_ledger WHERE qty > 1 UNION ALL SELECT b.ref_code, b.amt FROM beta_entry b JOIN r ON b.ref_code = r.id + 1) SELECT qty FROM r WHERE qty > 0
cases.why_it_might_slip: A recursive CTE's own name binds differently in its anchor and recursive arms.
cases.envelope_reason: recursive CTE refused: WITH RECURSIVE is not analysed here
